title: Relational knot boundary: the K1-K3 test and the width threshold
claim: Under relational semantics with the K1-K3 knot test, the two-loop knot is unique up to which contact value counts as made (the clause not-A or not-B or c); every knot is invisible in its smaller shadows; no 2-CNF with existentially quantified witnesses defines a knot; three-literal clauses with witnesses define the knot of any number of loops, which needs width n+1 without witnesses; and no affine relation is a knot. Proof 0009's executor rule supplies the gating literal that turns cross-wired 2-clause guards into the atom, and the earlier Lean kernel's erasure condition accepts the 2-CNF relation (A<->B) and (A->c).
failure_conditions: A relation on two loops and a contact other than the atom and its mirror passes K1-K3.
Some 2-CNF with existentially quantified witnesses defines a relation that passes K1-K3.
For some number of loops the three-literal witness chain does not define the knot.
The Lean kernel fails to compile with Lean 4.32.2 or depends on an axiom other than propext and Quot.sound.
A check in check.py accepts its deliberately wrong input.

thesis_alignment.scope: Relational semantics with K1-K3 (docs/KNOT_INTUITION.md): allowed states only, witnesses quantified away, no executor-supplied input, loop presence taken as given. 'proved_present' means a three-literal relation passes K1-K3 there; 'proved_absent' means no 2-CNF with witnesses passes K1-K3 (jointness fails because 2-CNF relations are determined by their pairs). Whether loop presence can be formed natively is open (KNOT-FOUNDATION-20261019-001B), so the native-formation safe flags stay false.

foundation_claim_scope: Definability of the knot relation in relational semantics with loop presence given. No native recurrence, composed topology, path, metric, complexity or physical claim.

validation.status: checked: Lean kernel accepted, check.py passed with every control rejecting its wrong input; no human or external review
validation.level: V2 trusted kernel: Lean 4.32.2 checks the two-loop theorems, the 2-CNF obstruction for any witness type, and the three-literal chain for every number of loops. V1: check.py re-derives the finite claims by its own enumeration, independently of tools/knotlab and of the Lean source.
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: the 2-CNF obstruction is Schaefer (1978) with Baker and Pixley (1975), and the chain is standard clause splitting; the delta is the K1-K3 definition and the two diagnoses of earlier project artifacts.
validation.independence: Written and checked in one session by Claude at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-19; no human or external review yet.
